notes: POC kicked off Aug 2024 focused on support-agent workflow + reranking for legal/explainability snippets.
Primary evaluation axis: structured JSON output reliability (schema adherence), and reliable tool-calling for downstream actions (ticket creation, DB writes).
Initial tests (Aug-Sep): Redwood good on latency and cost estimates; customer liked batching and KV caching proposals.

Nov 2024: customer noticed regressions vs incumbent (KestrelAI) after model swap in Redwood hosted catalog — generated malformed JSON (missing 'actions' array) and inconsistent function call signatures.
Regressions caused downstream pipeline failures in staging; engineering had to add brittle parsing workarounds to maintain flow.
SE tried model-config tweaks (temperature, structured output schema + chain-of-thought suppression) but reliability did not reach incumbent baseline in 2-week A/B run.
Customer quote (from Nov 12 call): 'We can't risk putting this in front of agents — too many misfires and we lose trust.'
Security team opened additional items: proof of data residency for PII, KMS integration details; Redwood provided draft answers but SSO/SAML cert exchange delayed by their IdP migration.
Late Dec: internal champion (Dir. of AI Ops) moved to a different role; no clear successor to push procurement.
Jan 2025: Procurement signaled budget freeze for FY25 until vendor consolidation decisions are revisited; they reverted traffic to incumbent and closed POC as 'failed to meet quality baseline'.

Competitive takeaway: KestrelAI has a slightly older but very stable structured-output model and a tested tool-calling shim that fit their workflows — they prioritized correctness over token-cost savings.

Redwood strengths noted: cleaner cost model, better latency on bursty queries, strong observability suggestions in Console. Weakness: structured-output regressions and function-call reliability during this POC.
Action history: multiple follow-ups 2024-11 through 2025-01, low responsiveness from procurement after budget freeze, final debrief call 2025-01-20 where customer confirmed cold stop.
Jira tickets attached list specific failures (RB-1129 malformed JSON on 'create_ticket' call; RB-1183 unexpected extra fields in 'entities' array).

AE notes: keep momentum on model-fix rollout and automated structured-output evals; ask Product to prioritize regression fixes and provide deterministic schema-testing harness to present at re‑engage.

Suggested next steps: 90-day re-engagement email with concrete regression metrics, invite to private beta of structured-output stability patch, request reference benchmark vs KestrelAI on customer's sample prompts.
